title: Magnetic or not? Sorting things with a fridge magnet
examples: What things stick to a magnet?
Why does a magnet not stick to a drinks can?

groups.label: Magnetic
groups.ask: What things stick to a magnet?

explain.say: Grab a fridge magnet and go on a hunt around your home! Some things snap onto it with a click, and some just ignore it. Let's sort what we find into two groups.

draw.text: Magnetic or not? Sorting things with a fridge magnet

groups.label: Magnetic
groups.ask: What things stick to a magnet?

explain.say: See the Magnetic group lighting up? A paper clip, an iron nail, a steel spoon and the fridge door all stick. Magnetic means a magnet pulls it. All of these have iron in them, and steel is mostly iron. Can you find one more magnetic thing near you?

groups.label: Magnetic
groups.ask: What things stick to a magnet?

explain.say: Now Not magnetic glows. Wood, plastic and glass never stick to a magnet. But look: a drinks can and a gold ring are metal, and they do not stick either! Did that surprise you?

groups.label: Magnetic
groups.ask: What things stick to a magnet?

explain.say: Here is why. See Can is aluminium lighting up? Magnets only pull strongly on a few metals: iron, nickel and cobalt. A drinks can is aluminium and a ring is gold, with no iron, so the magnet cannot grab them. Which metal does a magnet love most?

explain.say: So not every metal is magnetic, only iron, nickel and cobalt! Brilliant hunting! Wow fact: recycling centres use giant magnets to pull steel cans out of the rubbish, while aluminium cans are pushed out by a different machine.

faq.q: What things stick to a magnet?
faq.a: Things containing iron, nickel or cobalt stick to a magnet, such as paper clips, iron nails, steel spoons, steel cans and fridge doors.
No. Only a few metals, mainly iron, nickel and cobalt, and steel which is mostly iron, are pulled strongly by magnets. Aluminium, copper, gold and silver are not.

faq.q: Why does a magnet not stick to a drinks can?
faq.a: Most drinks cans are made of aluminium, a metal with no iron in it, so a magnet does not pull it. Some food tins are steel, and those do stick.

faq.q: Can a magnet work through paper?
faq.a: Yes. A magnet's pull passes through paper, cloth, plastic and even water. That is how a fridge magnet holds a drawing to the door.

faq.q: How do recycling centres use magnets?
faq.a: Big magnets pull steel cans and other iron-rich metal out of mixed rubbish, so it can be melted down and reused.
asks: Why are magnets used in recycling?

facts: Iron, nickel and cobalt are the common metals strongly attracted to magnets; aluminium, copper and gold are not.
Recycling plants use magnets to separate steel from other waste.
